forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred south of WA extends a ridge over most of SA. The high will move slowly eastwards during the week. A trough over inland WA will move over SA later in the week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated light morning showers about windward coasts and ranges of the southern agricultural area. Showers and isolated thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, tending southeast to northeasterly in the west, fresh near the coast during the afternoon and evening.

Patchy early morning frost about the South East districts. Showers and thunderstorms in the west. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to northeasterly winds, fresh near the coast during the afternoon and early evening.

Isolated light morning showers about central and eastern parts of the agricultural area. Showers and thunderstorms in the west. Maximum temperatures above average in the east and near the coast but below average elsewhere. Northeasterly winds.

text.p: Showers and isolated thunderstorms extending across most parts, clearing from the west during the evening. Maximum temperatures below average in the far west but above average elsewhere. Northeasterly winds, tending northwesterly in the west ahead of a southwesterly change in the far west.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: mostly less than 2 mm about the agricultural area and eastern parts of the North East Pastoral district, but isolated falls of 2 to 5 mm are possible. Generally 5 to 15 mm is expected about most remaining parts, increasing to 15 to 30 mm west of about Coober Pedy to Ceduna. Local falls of 30 to 60 mm are likely with thunderstorms in the far west and isolated higher falls are possible.
